column1: # THE THREE DEFECTS, MEASURED, AND THEIR COMMON ROOT CAUSE.
# DEFECT 1 -- THE PARENT PATH IS DUPLICATED
# The parent and CORRECTION03 both carry TWO terminal closes.
# CORRECTION01 and CORRECTION02 carry exactly one.
# DEFECT 2 -- THE PARENT C1/C2/C3 CARRY NO ACT TRAILER
# DEFECT 3 -- THE SAME DEFECT, REPRODUCED INSIDE CORRECTION03
# CORRECTION03 committed its own terminal close, then recorded the
# re-executed receipt outcome in a further commit, then committed a
# further close. Its range therefore contains TWO CLOSEs.
#   => REASON=expected exactly 1 CLOSE commit in range, found 2
# AND the earlier close has ACT-id DESCENDANTS, so rule 6 also fails:
#   commit <sha> after CLOSE still carries ACT: <id>;
#   ACT must not continue past CLOSE
#   rule 4  exactly ONE ACT-Phase: CLOSE in FIRST..CLOSE, and it is
#           the LAST commit of the range;
#   rule 6  NO commit DESCENDING FROM the CLOSE may carry ACT:<id>.
# A receipt that must be recorded AFTER the close therefore cannot be
# recorded with the ACT id, and cannot be recorded BEFORE the close
#   THE ACT'S PATH ENDS AT ITS TERMINAL CLOSE; THE CLOSE IS THE LAST
#   COMMIT CARRYING THE ACT ID; AND EVERYTHING AFTER IT IS AN
#   ORDINARY COMMIT WITH NO ACT TRAILER AT ALL.
